core_obligations: Retain the disjoint colour sets, rainbow ideal definition, all saturated product cells, labels, modules and signed differential.
Retain the full Example 5.3, its native TikZ square and full-box exactness statement used by Proposition 5.4.
Retain degree restrictions and Fact 1, then full Proposition 5.4 saturation argument yielding the p+n+2 homology gap.

Count whole Theorem 5.5 once; Proposition 5.4, Fact 1, all supports and later corollaries count zero. Remark 5.6 is not a dependency and is omitted.
proof_roadmap: The saturated product-of-simplices cells produce a linear free cellular complex.
Full-box exactness and saturation force every minimal-degree cycle to bound, leaving homology only in degrees at least p+n+2.
A degree-preserving comparison to a linear minimal resolution is successively an isomorphism by generator-degree injectivity and cokernel/homology induction.
difficulty_reason: H2: the current author core proves that saturation forces minimal-degree cycles to bound, hence the homology gap p+n+2 (Proposition 5.4), then uses a degree-controlled comparison map and cokernel induction to identify the explicit saturated-cell complex with the minimal free resolution (Theorem 5.5). These are retained nonroutine connections between combinatorial saturation and graded homological algebra, not an invocation of a general cellular-resolution criterion alone.
